topic: Matrix Multiplication as Composition of Linear Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Geometric View of a Matrix
lecture_lines: Matrices are functions that transform vectors.
Imagine a plane transforming under a matrix.
The unit square moves to a parallelogram.
animations: Show unit vectors i-hat and j-hat: #FF0000, #00FF00.
Animate transformation of i-hat and j-hat: #FF0000, #00FF00.

sections.title: Defining Composition: One Step After Another
lecture_lines: Apply two transformations one after another.
First apply A, then apply B.
This composition is denoted as B(Av).

sections.title: The 'Aha!' Moment: Matrix Multiplication
lecture_lines: Matrix multiplication BA represents this composition.
We apply B to the columns of A.
This maps the transformation steps perfectly.
The product BA simplifies sequential movement.
This is the beauty of matrix algebra.
animations: Animate transformation of result by A: #FF00FF.

sections.title: Visual Synthesis: The Sequential Path
lecture_lines: Watch the vector move through two transformations.
First it changes under A, then B.
The matrix BA performs both at once.

sections.title: Closing: Why Order Matters
lecture_lines: Order matters: AB does not equal BA.
Rotating then scaling changes the result.
Scaling then rotating creates a different pose.
